name: Kumano Kodo Nakahechi (熊野古道 中辺路)
why: The old pilgrim road to Kumano Hongu Taisha: two days of stone steps, cedar forest and small oji shrines, with a night in a mountain village inn.
book: No permit. Book the inn in Chikatsuyu early (Kumano Travel, the tourism bureau's booking site). Bus from Kii-Tanabe station to the Takijiri stop. A daily luggage shuttle runs along the route.
water: Fill up at the Kumano Kodo Kan at Takijiri and at your inn. Day 2 has no restaurants: carry lunch and 1.5-2 litres. Stream water is untested.
dangers: Wet stone steps and roots: most injuries are slips, often on the old cobbles.
Typhoons and heavy rain cause landslides and floods: check the forecast every day.
Mamushi pit vipers, hornets (worst in autumn), leeches and ticks: long sleeves and trousers.
Day 2 is 24.5 km: valleys get dark early, carry a headlamp.
turnaround: On day 2, if you are not at Tsugizakura-oji by 10:00, take the bus from Nonaka Ipposugi to Hosshinmon-oji or Hongu.

points.name: Takijiri-oji
points.note: The shrine where the mountain route begins, by the Takijiri bus stop and the Kumano Kodo Kan information centre. The path climbs steeply straight away.

points.name: Chikatsuyu-oji
points.note: Night 1 in Chikatsuyu village, after 13.3 km and about 1,000 m of climb. Inns serve dinner around 18:00.

points.name: Hosshinmon-oji
points.note: The 'gate of awakening', traditionally the entrance to Hongu's sacred area. The last 7 km run through forest, tea fields and hamlets.

points.name: Kumano Hongu Taisha
points.note: The grand shrine, up its long flight of stone steps. The Hongu Heritage Centre and the buses to Tanabe and Shingu are across the road.
